:::{#exm-aic-lrt}
#### The significance levels implied by AIC and BIC

Suppose model A in @exm-aic-bic-compare is nested in model B,
so model B adds $k = 2$ parameters.
The likelihood ratio statistic is

$$
\ba
G^2
&= 2\paren{-118.5 - (-120.0)}
&& \text{(definition of } G^2 \text{)} \\
&= 2 \cdot 1.5
&& \text{(subtract)} \\
&= 3
&& \text{(multiply)}
\ea
$$

By @thm-aic-lrt,
AIC prefers model B only if $G^2 > 2k = 4$,
and BIC (with $n = 100$) only if $G^2 > 2 \logf{100} \approx 9.21$.
Since $G^2 = 3$ clears neither threshold,
both criteria prefer model A,
matching @exm-aic-bic-compare.

Under $H_0$ (the $k = 2$ extra parameters are zero),
$G^2$ approximately follows a $\chi^2_2$ distribution,
which is the [exponential distribution](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-exponential) with mean 2,
so $\P(\chi^2_2 > c) = \expf{-c/2}$.
Choosing model B whenever AIC prefers it
therefore acts like a likelihood ratio test at level

$$
\P(\chi^2_2 > 4) = \expf{-2} \approx 0.135
$$

and choosing by BIC acts like a test at level

$$
\ba
\P(\chi^2_2 > 2 \logf{100})
&= \expf{-\logf{100}}
&& \text{(} \chi^2_2 \text{ tail probability)} \\
&= \frac{1}{100}
&& \text{(} \expf{-\logf{a}} = 1/a \text{)}
\ea
$$

AIC is a more lenient threshold than the conventional $\alpha = 0.05$,
which is one reason it tends to select larger models,
while BIC's implied level shrinks as $n$ grows.

:::
